note: Questions 23 and 24 distinguish the Chinese macrolanguage (zho), Mandarin (cmn), and Yue (yue), and discuss common written context. Traditional/Simplified is a separate script distinction. Do not infer one variety from an umbrella label. This verifies the macrolanguage scope, not every boundary in the broader Sinitic grouping.

Original historical research distinguishes regional Mandarin varieties from the codified standard, explaining northern dialect and Beijing pronunciation inputs. Do not treat Mandarin as synonymous with all Chinese.
The Norwegian Language Council explicitly identifies Bokmål and Nynorsk as the two Norwegian written standards.
PCC guidance distinguishes the Serbo-Croatian macrolanguage code and the separate standard-language codes for Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin, and Serbian. This supports scope, not synonymy.
PCC confirms Bosnian as a distinct standard-language identifier (bos) and its use in written records. The draft is generic and spoken usage was not checked here.
OMG identifies UML as a standard for visualizing and documenting software and systems, including structure and behavior. The actual draft describes the language, not the skill of using it.
